# Every normal stress can fail the proposed source-to-contact convex order

This is an exact counterexample to a convex-order strengthening of the
joint hinge moment equations. It uses an actual full-dimensional convex
body, and classifies ALL of its global hinge minimizers and ALL normal
joint stresses. It is not an OC counterexample: its covering cap budget
is one half of total mass, above the OC threshold in these dimensions.

## 1. The rational mixed body and the optimization problem

Let n=2,d=1 and P={0,1}^2. Write

    epsilon_z=(-1)^(z_1+z_2), h_z=epsilon_z/4,
    K_z=[h_z-1,h_z+1].

Let C be the convex hull in R^2 x R of these four lifted intervals.
Its projection is the unit square. Because every z in P is an extreme
point of that square, C_z is exactly K_z. The square has no other
integer points. Thus C induces exactly these four positive interval
fibers, each of length two, and M=H_1(S)=8. The hull has nonempty
three-dimensional interior: two different points in one interval and
points over three affinely independent base vertices span R^3.

Consider covers by N=2 closed ambient caps with unit continuous
normals, each of mixed mass at most tau M=4, where tau=1/2. The caps

    H_+={x>=0}, H_-={x<=0}                             (1)

are feasible. Their masses are four each and their hinge integrals are

    Psi_+=Psi_-=(1/2)sum_z(1+h_z)^2=17/8,
    Psi=17/4.                                         (2)

All boundaries are four isolated section points and have H_1-mass
zero. Coverage nevertheless includes every boundary point.

## 2. Complete classification of global minimizers

First, on ANY interval [h-1,h+1], two unit-normal affine caps covering
the interval have total hinge integral at least one. If the normals
have the same sign, at least one cap covers the whole interval, and
its hinge integral is at least two. If the normals are opposite, write
the margins x-p and q-x. If p<=q, choose t in [p,q]; pointwise

    (x-p)_++(q-x)_+>=|x-t|.

The integral of the last expression on the interval is at least one,
with equality only at t=h. If p>q, coverage forces the interval to
lie entirely on one side of the uncovered open gap (q,p), so one cap
covers the whole interval and again its hinge integral is at least
two. A cap covering the whole interval always has hinge integral at
least two, since its threshold cannot be beyond the nearest endpoint.

It follows that any two-cap cover with a wholly assigned fiber costs
at least 2+1+1+1=5. The feasible value 17/4 is smaller. Thus every
global minimizer has opposite cap signs and both caps cut every
interval properly. Since the caps cover S and their mass sum is at
most M, their intersection has zero mixed mass. On each interval the
opposing thresholds must therefore coincide. Calling their common
threshold t_z, both caps' affine base traces agree on P, so

    t_z=b-a dot z

for one affine function. The hinge objective is then exactly

    sum_z integral_(K_z) |x-t_z| dx
       =4+sum_z(t_z-h_z)^2,                            (3)

because all four cuts are proper. The checkerboard array h is
orthogonal to every affine function on P:

    sum_z h_z=sum_z z_1 h_z=sum_z z_2 h_z=0.

Thus (3) equals 4+sum h_z^2+sum t_z^2 and is uniquely minimized by
t_z=0 for every z. This affine trace is realized by a=0,b=0 and is
unique since P affinely spans R^2. Consequently EVERY global minimizer
is (1), up to exchanging the two cap labels. The proof does not merely
show stationarity or local minimality.

## 3. All joint source/contact measures at this minimum

Use the joint Fritz--John notation from
`candidate de8d1a3251731edd`.
Each fiber's whole-cover margin is min_(x in K_z)|x|=0, uniquely at
x_z=0. Since 0 is interior to every interval, the only dual-optimal
cover weights are

    lambda_z+=(1/2), lambda_z-=(1/2).                  (4)

Both sections are proper interior points, so their effective section
densities are exactly one. Write alpha=alpha_0 and let r_+,r_- be the
nonnegative cap-budget multipliers. The source integer marginals are

    sigma_+(z)=alpha(1+h_z)+r_+,
    sigma_-(z)=alpha(1-h_z)+r_-.                       (5)

The contact marginals for the two caps are the SAME measure

    omega(z)=eta_z/2.                                 (6)

The mass equations force r_+=r_-=r. The integer moment equations,
together with the checkerboard orthogonality, then give

    omega(z)=A+s epsilon_z,
    A=alpha+r, |s|<=A.                                (7)

Indeed every scalar array on the four square vertices with zero
total and zero two first moments is a multiple of epsilon. Formula
(7) is precisely the nonnegativity condition on omega. Conversely,
every alpha,r>=0 with A>0 and every |s|<=A gives a full joint stress:
take eta_z=2omega(z), the weights (4), contacts x_z=0, and the proper
section densities one. The continuous equation follows because
m_+=Psi_+, m_-=-Psi_- and all section/contact x-moments vanish.
The sphere multipliers are -alpha Psi_i; lambda stationarity holds
because both margins are zero at the unique contact. Thus (5)-(7)
are not abstract moment-matching examples; they describe actual
minimizer stresses.

In particular normal stresses alpha=1 exist, for example r=s=0,
eta_z=2. This also follows from the separately proved d=1 normality
theorem, but no such theorem is needed to certify this example.

## 4. The exact convex-order obstruction

For finite measures on R^2, write sigma>=cx omega if

    integral phi d sigma>=integral phi d omega

for every finite convex function phi:R^2->R. Our source/contact
measures have equal masses and first moments, as required by (15)--(16).

On P={0,1}^2, convex-order domination between measures of the same
mass forces their equality. For each p in P, the function

    phi_p(z)=max(0,1-q_p(z)),
    q_p(z)=sum_k[(1-p_k)z_k+p_k(1-z_k)]

is convex, because q_p is globally affine. On P it is the indicator
of the single vertex p. Thus sigma>=cx omega implies
sigma(p)>=omega(p) at every p; equality of total masses then forces
equality at all four vertices.

Consequently both proposed comparisons

    sigma_+>=cx omega, sigma_->=cx omega               (8)

can hold only if sigma_+=omega=sigma_-. By (5), this is impossible
whenever alpha>0, since h_z is never zero. Hence NO normal joint
stress at ANY global minimizer satisfies the desired convex-order
comparison for every cap.

There is a quantitative finite certificate. For alpha>0,

    sum_z min(sigma_+(z),sigma_-(z))=4A-alpha,
    sum_z omega(z)=4A.

Therefore at some p,

    omega(p)-min(sigma_+(p),sigma_-(p))>=alpha/4>0.

The corresponding function phi_p violates one of (8) by at least
alpha/4. This includes arbitrary r>=0 and arbitrary contact choices
s, not just the explicit r=s=0 stress.

If alpha=0, (8) DOES hold by taking s=0 and any r>0: the two source
section marginals and the contact marginal are identical uniform
measures of weight r on P. This abnormal comparison carries no
objective-cap source mass. Thus allowing alpha=0 does not rescue the
normal source transport sought for a hinge-objective estimate; but
the example does not refute the bare assertion that some abnormal
stress might satisfy convex order.

## 5. Both affine-width normalizations have the same obstruction

For this same actual convex body,

    D_int=[-2,2], D_all=[-5/2,5/2].

The first assertion follows from the four interval lengths. For the
second, all of C lies between x=-5/4 and x=5/4, and both extremes
occur over the SAME real base (1/2,1/2): use the average of the upper
endpoints at (0,0),(1,1), and the average of the lower endpoints at
(0,1),(1,0). Their difference is 5/2.

More generally, for ANY fixed one-dimensional width body D=[-W,W],
W>0, the normalization h_D(u)=1 makes u=+1/W or -1/W. The quotient
hinge objective is exactly 1/W times the unit-normal objective, so
the geometric global minimizers remain uniquely (1), up to exchange.
Each proper section's coarea mass is now W. The two source marginals
are therefore

    alpha(1+h_z)+W r_+, alpha(1-h_z)+W r_-.

Their common contact marginal still forces r_+=r_-. Every argument
in Section 4 applies with A=alpha+Wr. Thus no normal stress has both
source-to-contact convex-order comparisons under either D_int or
D_all normalization. The example directly addresses the attempted
integer-target transport replacement of D_all by D_int; it is not
an artifact of Euclidean normalization.

## 6. Scope of what is falsified

The counterexample is compatible, rational, full dimensional, attained,
and uses actual contacts and actual active equal-budget caps. It shows
that no universal choice of a NORMAL minimizer stress can strengthen
the joint integer first-moment identities to source-dominates-contact
convex order. Accordingly, Strassen-type integer-target martingale
decomposition cannot be inferred from those identities, even by
optimizing the available normal stress or choosing a different global
minimizer in this example.

The cap budget here is 1/2, whereas the n=2,d=1 OC target is 1/8.
No assertion about a hypothetical sub-OC covering budget follows from
this example alone. No OC counterexample or minimizing-body example
is asserted, and no arbitrary-measure construction replaces the
explicit attained cap optimization above.
